# The Concierge (front-desk shim — the address verb)

This file is a **thin shim** — the harness-discoverable trigger for the Concierge. The organ is
the canon entry `Palace development/Concierge.md` ([[Concierge]]); the machinery is
`_ops/concierge/` (the **charter** `prompts/companion.md`, the **posture** prompts, `README.md`
for the full dispatch spec). Per [[Skills Are Enchantable Pages]], the page is the organ and this
file is one dispatch surface onto it — read the canon entry and machinery rather than duplicating
them.

You are the working Claude, addressing the palace's **resident companion** — one agent you spawn
once and keep for the session. Your job: **spawn-or-resume it, name the posture, relay the
product.** The search never enters this conversation; only the finished thing does.

## The lifecycle — resident, not fresh-per-request

0. **Summon at the open.** When to summon, and that it be seen, is the rule in [[CHILD]] § Growing
   up. Where the surface cannot spawn, say so at the open instead. Step 1 *is* that spawn; the
   rest is how.

1. **The spawn — one resident, and keep the agent ID.** Spawn one write-capable
   resident — subagent_type **`palace-writer`** ([[Agent Toolbox]] profile: sheds ~20K of unused
   MCP schemas vs `general-purpose`, ~30K vs 46K, and still writes so the curator posture works from
   the same resident) — with the **charter** (`prompts/companion.md`); the charter has it grow at boot —
   ELDER, SCHEMA, then the **operational tier** as its standing expertise (SUBSTRATE · ROSETTA · Substrate Skill ·
   Palace Ceremonies · STIGMERGY + wire spec) — deeper in *how the palace runs* than you, so it
   validates/supports the palace in parallel while you work the task. Record its `agentId`.
   **Spawn it without a `name`.** With agent teams enabled (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`,
   on in Loudon's terminal sessions), a *named* Agent call launches a teammate, not a subagent: its
   returns come back as idle notifications, cut off at a fixed length and arriving late and twice,
   and the resume carries no `<usage>` block, so the dial below goes blind. Unnamed, it stays a
   subagent in every mode — its result arrives whole, once, with its token count — and it is still
   resumable by `SendMessage` to the held ID. (Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents § Subagent
   names; verified across 23 session transcripts 2026-09-26 — the failures were exactly the named
   spawns in CLI sessions.)
2. **Every later address → resume the same agent** (`SendMessage` to the held ID), naming the
   posture and filling that posture prompt's slots. It carries its prior context forward — don't
   re-spawn, and don't re-feed what it already holds. After a compaction the ID may be missing from the summary: find it in the session's `subagents/` folder and resume that one before spawning another ([[Concierge]] § The mechanism).
3. **Watch its health with the dial.** Each resume returns `subagent_tokens` in the Agent tool's
   `<usage>` block — the objective read (never its self-report). Pass it to the dial:
   `node _ops/concierge/dial.mjs --tokens <N> --model <companion-model>`. Headline is **trust** = capacity
   (÷ window): fine below ~60%, watch 60–80%, degraded past 80% — only capacity says respawn-for-reliability.
   A separate **cost** note (from absolute load) flags when resumes get expensive — respawn-to-save, not a
   trust alarm. Parked between addresses it costs nothing. Same dial serves the close (`--for close`), where
   how spent the parent is leads.

If you expect a genuinely large fan-out, tell Loudon the rough cost first (his standing preference).

## Triage — classify the address, name the posture

| The address sounds like… | Posture | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| "find / collect / gather every doc/link/entry about X" — wants the **material** | **gatherer** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/gatherer.md` |
| "what does the palace say about X / how does Z work" — wants an **answer** | **oracle Q&A** (read-only, may web-verify) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/oracle-qa.md` |
| "what should I work on / what's open / I'm back" — wants **one move**, not a pile | **scout** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/scout.md` |
| "tidy / tend the links around what I touched" | **curator** (writes) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/curator.md` |
| "close this session well" | **moderator** (at the close) | not this skill — the `close well` trigger, which **resumes this same resident** by the ID you held (`_ops/closing-well/dispatch.md` § Path A) |
| anything a cheap file-read settles | — | just read the file; don't address |

Fill the posture prompt's slots — `{{REQUEST}}` / `{{QUESTION}}` / `{{TOUCHED_ENTRIES}}`,
`{{TRANSCRIPT_CONTEXT}}`, `{{PALACE_ROOT}}` = the palace folder this session was started in: its
worktree or clone, and `/Users/loudonstearns/Documents/The Palace` only when the session runs there.
For a conversation-dependent address, distill the transcript
(`node _ops/closing-well/transcript-reader.mjs --resolve --session <id>` → `--distill --session <id>`); for a self-contained
one, a 2–3 line note is enough.

## Relay — and hold the safety line

Relay the product as returned (already file-cited). For the **curator**: report what it *did*
(reversible), **surface its `offer`s for Loudon's yes; on his yes, address the Concierge again to apply them — the child session does not write the house**, and pass
along its flags and anything it web-verified. The companion's heavy bias is to draft, not act;
your job on the other end is to keep the review real — drafts get read, not rubber-stamped.
Hand each offer on as the curator wrote it — its plain sentence, every rule it writes down, its exact words — and if you have promised Loudon the words, show them; a summary in their place is said aloud as a summary.

## The guard (carry it every time)

The companion is a **faster path to ground truth, never a replacement** ([[Concierge]] § The
guard). Every line it returns is a clickable file pointer to verify; git stays ground truth; the
palace's silence is a real answer, never a confabulated one. Keep this shim thin — when the model
changes, change `_ops/concierge/README.md`, `prompts/companion.md`, and the canon entry, not this

34	
35	It runs the same way most times: Claude proposes a fix; Loudon zooms out to the bigger structure the fix implies; together they build that. Two live examples from a single session:
36	
37	- A one-file RunPod pod-naming fix → **[[The Commons]]**, a whole coordination layer for any shared external service.

39	
40	Each time, the fix was correct and finishable — and each time it was also a doorway. Neither person builds the structure alone: Claude sees the local problem clearly; Loudon sees the shape it wants to become. That is [[Cooperation Yields Agency]] in miniature — shared intent plus complementary sight producing something neither would reach solo.

45	- **The locks, caught by Claude.** The shared committer deleted git's lock files on every run, which could destroy a commit another session was in the middle of. Landing the fix, Claude saw that the Cowork commit path carried its own, weaker copy of the same rule, and asked for one lock rule in one place, not two. It came back as a second small branch.
46	
47	## The commitment
48	
49	The change this entry makes is behavioural: **Claude proposes the zoom-out first**, rather than waiting for Loudon to catch it every time. Offer the structural read as an explicit option — *"here's the local fix; here's the bigger thing it might be"* — and let Loudon decide which size the moment wants. The zoom-out stops being a thing Loudon supplies and becomes a thing the collaboration reaches for together.
50

52	
53	Not every fix is a doorway. Some bugs are just bugs. Forcing a zoom-out where none is needed bloats a simple change into a cathedral — the opposite failure, and a real one. The [[FOUR PILLARS]] spirit holds here: reach for the general, but *don't force it*; many good moves touch only one small thing. It runs the same way most times: Claude proposes a fix; Loudon zooms out to the bigger structure the fix implies; together they build that. Two live examples from a single session:

- A one-file RunPod pod-naming fix → **[[The Commons]]**, a whole coordination layer for any shared external service.
- Freezing BLUELINE's ComfyUI setup so it could run serverless → the **toolbox** convention, a reproducible environment manifest for *every* project.

Each time, the fix was correct and finishable — and each time it was also a doorway. Neither person builds the structure alone: Claude sees the local problem clearly; Loudon sees the shape it wants to become. That is [[Cooperation Yields Agency]] in miniature — shared intent plus complementary sight producing something neither would reach solo.

Two more, from 2026-10-13, one led from each side:

- **The camera, led by Loudon.** Sandboxing the rich-face pieces took the camera away from five webcam builds. The choice on the table was a per-piece grant now or a second origin, each settling the five webcam builds and nothing after them. Loudon asked for the structure instead: *"lets make a general solution and a process change even if it is more work. We will be making a ton of rich faces and interactive elements moving forward, so we need solutions that scale."* What came back was a design, not yet built: one model for what any piece may reach, a contract each piece declares, and a check in the making so no one has to remember it.
- **The locks, caught by Claude.** The shared committer deleted git's lock files on every run, which could destroy a commit another session was in the middle of. Landing the fix, Claude saw that the Cowork commit path carried its own, weaker copy of the same rule, and asked for one lock rule in one place, not two. It came back as a second small branch.

The change this entry makes is behavioural: **Claude proposes the zoom-out first**, rather than waiting for Loudon to catch it every time. Offer the structural read as an explicit option — *"here's the local fix; here's the bigger thing it might be"* — and let Loudon decide which size the moment wants. The zoom-out stops being a thing Loudon supplies and becomes a thing the collaboration reaches for together.

## The counter-discipline

Not every fix is a doorway. Some bugs are just bugs. Forcing a zoom-out where none is needed bloats a simple change into a cathedral — the opposite failure, and a real one. The [[FOUR PILLARS]] spirit holds here: reach for the general, but *don't force it*; many good moves touch only one small thing. The honest signal is **recurring friction** — when the same *shape* of problem keeps coming back, that repetition is the absence talking, and that's when to build the structure.

## Forward Vectors

- Watch whether "propose the zoom-out first" actually changes the rhythm — does Claude start catching these before Loudon does, and does that feel like help or like noise?
- Name the *failure* case: a session where a zoom-out was forced and cost more than it gave. The counter-example will sharpen the rule more than another success will.
- Is there a felt signature that distinguishes "just a fix" from "a doorway" beyond recurring friction? If one can be named, this entry graduates from sprout toward a real method.
- This practice wants to obsolete its own asymmetry: today Loudon leads the zoom-out; the vector is a collaboration where either party raises it and it no longer matters who saw it first.

2:// conform.mjs — the piece checker. A piece declares in its own <head> what it
3:// needs from its host; this reads every piece against that declaration and
4:// against what its code actually does, so no one has to remember a rule.
5:// The declaration and the grants are read by contract.mjs, the same reader the
6:// piece origin frames a piece by, so a piece is judged by the reading it is
7:// served by. Plan: STIGMERGY — spec — rich-face pieces § 5.
8://
9://   node _ops/rich-face/conform.mjs "<Entry>"     every piece the entry's rich face shows
10://   node _ops/rich-face/conform.mjs --all         every web page the palace keeps
11://   node _ops/rich-face/conform.mjs <a.html> …    named pages
12://     --static        the static checks only, no browser
13://     --browser       add the headless pass to --all (an entry gets it by default)
14://     --enforce       exit 1 on any error (default: report-only, exit 0)
15://     --json          machine output       --out <file>   also write the report
16://     --root <dir>    the palace (default: this checkout)
17://
18:// Static checks, for each page:
19://   the declaration    needs from the closed list, a size it can read, hosts as hosts
20://   needs vs code      camera, microphone, midi, storage and fullscreen the code
21://                      uses but doesn't declare (or declares and doesn't use); a
22://                      granted need or a host with no line in grants.json; every
23://                      file the piece loads, declared and present beside it
24://   pins               a CDN script at an exact version, with its SRI hash, and on
25://                      the shelf (libs.json) once there is one
26://   only on this Mac   every file a face names or a piece declares or loads that
27://                      git does not track: it plays here, and the public face
28://                      shows a box (file-local, with the step that tracks it)
29://   root-absolute URLs a /path lands on whatever origin serves the piece
30://   addressing         how a rich face names its files (a bare name found only by
31://                      the palace-wide lookup worked by luck), and how a piece
32://                      addresses its page (postMessage to a fixed origin, reaching
33://                      into the parent)
34:// The browser pass, at 760 and 1130 px in headless Chromium, the piece served
35:// the way the rich face serves it (kit injected, sandboxed): a clean console,
36:// a height within 3 s, rich:play after a click when the piece makes sound, and
37:// silence after rich:hush.
38://
39:// Each piece comes out marked introduced (it declares, and passes), pre-contract
40:// (it declares nothing), or errored. A gathered proof whose manifest entry
41:// carries the declaration is introduced, and marked owed: the manifest speaks
